summary: PLS has a team of family lawyers, a free 15 minute call and a large review base. Conflicting offers and ratings, stray text and location errors weaken a firm that clients must trust.

findings.problem: The intro promises complimentary initial consultations, but the pricing section lists paid consultations at $349, $449 and $999. Two rating widgets show 5.0 and 4.7 based on 36 reviews.
findings.cost: A client who sees a free offer and then a fee, or two different ratings, stops trusting the page.
findings.fix: One clear consultation offer and one verified rating.

findings.problem: At least two review cards are empty, testimonials name a lawyer who has left the firm, and two negative reviews have no visible response.
findings.cost: Empty cards and unanswered complaints are the first thing a careful client notices.
findings.fix: A clean review wall with responses to every review.

findings.problem: The Toronto page has a heading about Richmond Hill, the Barrie and Toronto addresses use the same map link, and the Sheppard office is called both Toronto and North York.
findings.cost: A client who cannot tell which office is theirs may go to the wrong place.
findings.fix: One verified address and map for each office.

findings.problem: Stray text shows: Slogan, Generic selectors, Post Type Selectors, imunify-bot-check, and underscore markup in headings. Two phone numbers (416 and 705) appear without explanation.
findings.cost: Leftover system text on a law firm page makes it look unmaintained.
findings.fix: A clean page with one phone number per location.

redesign: A consultation first page with one offer, one phone number per office and one verified rating.
A clean review wall and a short booking form linked to your calendar.
